ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is the comparative form of 'little' (amount)? (1 mark)
   A. littler
   B. less
   C. more little
   D. least

2. About how long is a Grade 4 narrative composition? (1 mark)
   A. 60 to 80 words
   B. 5 words
   C. 10 words
   D. 1000 words

3. Which detail uses the sense of smell? (1 mark)
   A. I saw a table.
   B. I could smell fresh bread.
   C. I heard a bell.
   D. I touched a wall.

4. Quantifiers: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. How many book are there?
   B. How much books are there?
   C. How many books are there?
   D. How much book are there?

5. Which sentence shows a habit in the present tense? (1 mark)
   A. I was asking my mother.
   B. I always ask my mother before opening a new page.
   C. I asked my mother yesterday.
   D. I had asked my mother.

6. Which word has the soft buzzing sound /ʒ/ in the middle? (1 mark)
   A. jug
   B. bridge
   C. television
   D. yam

7. What is a graded reader? (1 mark)
   A. A dictionary
   B. A newspaper advert
   C. A test paper
   D. A book written at a level of difficulty suited to certain readers

8. To retell a story, which things should you say? (1 mark)
   A. Only the last word
   B. Who, where, what happened and how it ended
   C. The page numbers
   D. Only the title

9. Which verb is NOT normally used in the progressive form? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. know
   C. write
   D. sing

10. Which sentence has the right capital letters and full stop? (1 mark)
   A. Akinyi lives near River Nzoia.
   B. Akinyi lives near river nzoia,
   C. akinyi lives near River Nzoia!
   D. akinyi lives near river nzoia

11. Which of these is a proper noun? (1 mark)
   A. hill
   B. river
   C. town
   D. Mombasa

12. What is fertilizer used for? (1 mark)
   A. To dig the soil
   B. To store water
   C. To kill birds
   D. To help plants grow

13. Which word has the vowel glide /ʊə/? (1 mark)
   A. manure
   B. harvest
   C. maize
   D. plough

14. What is reader's theatre? (1 mark)
   A. Acting a play with full costumes
   B. Copying a script
   C. Reading parts from a script with only your voice, without costumes or sets
   D. Silent reading

15. What is a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. A list of facts
   B. A description of an object
   C. A story that tells what happened in order
   D. A set of instructions

16. When should you use a simile? (1 mark)
   A. To help the reader picture something
   B. Only in questions
   C. Every second word
   D. Instead of full stops

17. Which word means 'to move from one person or place to another' (for example an illness)? (1 mark)
   A. signs
   B. diet
   C. spread
   D. cure

18. Which word is an adverb of place? (1 mark)
   A. soon
   B. always
   C. gently
   D. outside

19. Which sentence puts the comma after the opening phrase? (1 mark)
   A. In the morning, we do exercises.
   B. In the morning we, do exercises.
   C. In the morning we do, exercises.
   D. In, the morning we do exercises.

20. Which sentence has a comma before the spoken words? (1 mark)
   A. Mother said "Please close the door"
   B. Mother said. "Please close the door"
   C. Mother said, "Please close the door."
   D. Mother, said "Please close the door."

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Fill in much or many: (a) How ___ eggs? (b) How ___ sugar? (2 marks)

22. Compose a tongue twister with at least six words that contain the sound /w/. (3 marks)

23. Correct this sentence and explain: 'I don't have no seeds.' (3 marks)

24. Write three sentences about your family or school: one comparative, one superlative and one with two adjectives in the right order. (3 marks)

25. Explain why 'She asked where the clinic was?' is wrong and correct it. (3 marks)

26. Write one sentence using 'while' with the past progressive. (3 marks)

27. Correct the paragraph: 'last friday our class visited the museum. mr. juma told us about kenya.' (4 marks)

28. Explain how /v/ and /w/ are made differently. (2 marks)

29. Write three sentences about your classroom using some, any and many. (3 marks)

30. Write two sentences using 'compose' and 'reply'. (2 marks)

31. Explain why 'more better' is wrong. Give the correct form. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — less
   Little, less, least.

2. A — 60 to 80 words
   The design asks for about 60 to 80 words.

3. B — I could smell fresh bread.
   It describes something smelt.

4. C — How many books are there?
   Books are countable and plural.

5. B — I always ask my mother before opening a new page.
   'Always' and the simple present 'ask' show a habit.

6. C — television
   'Television' has /ʒ/. 'Jug' and 'bridge' have /ʤ/.

7. D — A book written at a level of difficulty suited to certain readers
   Graded readers are written at different reading levels.

8. B — Who, where, what happened and how it ended
   A retelling covers characters, place, events and ending.

9. B — know
   'Know' describes a state, not an action in progress.

10. A — Akinyi lives near River Nzoia.
   Names and the first word begin with capitals, and the statement ends with a full stop.

11. D — Mombasa
   Mombasa is the name of a particular town.

12. D — To help plants grow
   Fertilizer adds nutrients to soil.

13. A — manure
   'Manure' has the /ʊə/ sound, as in 'pure'.

14. C — Reading parts from a script with only your voice, without costumes or sets
   Reader's theatre uses voices only.

15. C — A story that tells what happened in order
   A narrative tells events in order.

16. A — To help the reader picture something
   A simile helps the reader imagine.

17. C — spread
   Germs spread from person to person.

18. D — outside
   'Outside' tells where.

19. A — In the morning, we do exercises.
   A comma follows the opening phrase.

20. C — Mother said, "Please close the door."
   A comma comes after 'said' before the spoken words.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) many (b) much
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: We watched worms wriggle when the wind whistled.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a sentence, 1 for at least six /w/ words, 1 for making sense.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: I don't have any seeds (or: I have no seeds). English uses only one negative word here.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct sentence, 2 marks for the explanation.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: My brother is taller than I am. He is the tallest boy in his class. He has a big round bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: It reports a question, so it is a statement and needs a full stop. Correct: She asked where the clinic was.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reason, 1 for correction, 1 for full stop.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Mother was cooking while I was doing my homework.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for while, 1 for was/were, 1 for verb-ing forms used correctly.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Last Friday our class visited the museum. Mr. Juma told us about Kenya.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for Last Friday, Mr. Juma, Kenya and correct full stops.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: For /v/ the upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes; for /w/ the lips are rounded and do not touch the teeth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: There are many desks in our classroom. We have some pictures on the wall. Is there any chalk?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: I will compose an email to my uncle. He will reply tomorrow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Better is already the comparative form, so we do not add more. The correct form is better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the reason and 1 mark for the correct form.
